coordinates.title: Enter or edit corners using the keyboard
coordinates.label: Corner coordinates
coordinates.help: One corner per line: longitude, latitude, using a decimal point. Enter at least three corners in order. Do not repeat the first corner at the end. Apply replaces the draft corners; Finish requests the assessment.
coordinates.invalid: Enter at least three lines with two valid numbers separated by a comma: longitude, latitude.

safety.title: Educational demo, not an official warning.
safety.description: Do not use this website as the sole basis for safety decisions. A low FWI does not mean it is safe. Consult official restrictions and warnings.
safety.providers: Requires internet and WebGL. The viewer uses external services. External providers receive requests for visible tiles. Production use requires reviewing terms and quotas. FWI values are fictitious and do not assess real risk.

project.title: Learning technology. Making our surroundings understandable.
project.introduction: SubegIA is a personal learning and portfolio project exploring how to present weather-related fire danger on a 3D map of Gipuzkoa. It is not intended to replace professionals, public authorities or official warnings.

explore.label: 01 / Explore
explore.title: The landscape, in three dimensions
explore.description: CesiumJS displays real terrain, mountains and valleys. You can draw an area and explore results by subarea based on the information available.

understand.label: 02 / Understand
understand.title: An explained index, not just a colour
understand.description: The aim is to show the FWI value, its category, date, source and limitations. Not to present a number as a certainty or as the probability of a fire occurring.

build.label: 03 / Build
build.title: An experience for learning
build.description: Angular, Spring Boot and geospatial visualisation form the first stage. Microservices and Spring AI will be added later as learning objectives.

project.statusNotice: Current status: experimental FWI calculations connected to the map, with subarea results and details. The initial view is an example. Local accuracy has not been validated.

science.title: What FWI means and how we calculate it
science.meaning: The Canadian Fire Weather Index (FWI) is a dimensionless index summarising weather conditions related to potential fire intensity. It is not an ignition probability or a prediction of a fire's path, and does not account for all fuels, terrain, exposed people or buildings.
science.inputs: We use hourly AROME HD model data from Open-Meteo's Historical Forecast API: temperature, relative humidity and 10 m wind at 11:00 UTC (noon CET standard time), plus rainfall over the preceding 24 hours. These are model estimates, not measurements on each plot.
science.method: Each day we update FFMC (fine fuel moisture), DMC (intermediate-depth organic matter) and DC (deep layers). These codes feed ISI (initial spread), BUI (available fuel) and finally FWI. Moisture states carry over to the following day.
science.initialization: The prototype reconstructs 365 days from initial FFMC 85, DMC 6 and DC 15. These are experimental assumptions, not measured states in Gipuzkoa. History reduces dependence on the starting point but does not establish local accuracy. Data gaps produce unavailable subareas, not zeros.
science.reading: We show the latest complete available day, which may precede today. Categories use EFFIS thresholds. Model cells are clipped to the selection; detailed 3D terrain does not imply equally detailed weather data. Always follow official restrictions and warnings.

howItWorks.title: From weather data to a visual reading.
howItWorks.introduction: The application explains its data and calculation method. Scientific calculations are not delegated to a language model.

select.label: Step 01
select.title: Select an area
select.description: Draw a polygon within Gipuzkoa. The backend validates coverage and matches it to AROME HD weather cells.

calculate.label: Step 02
calculate.title: Calculate the FWI
calculate.description: Spring Boot uses temperature, relative humidity, wind, rainfall and moisture history from Open-Meteo to calculate daily FWI.

explore.label: Step 03
explore.title: Explore and understand
explore.description: The map and panel display results, dates and unavailable areas. Select a subarea for details. This guidance does not replace official warnings.

howItWorks.sourceLink: Read the explanation of FWI on EFFIS

limitations.title: A detailed visualisation is not an exact prediction.
limitations.introduction: SubegIA is an experimental demonstration. No local accuracy percentage has been established. These are some reasons why its results must not be used as the sole basis for decisions about safety or land management.

data.label: Data
data.title: Models are estimates
data.description: Weather estimated by a model may differ from what happens on a particular plot. Quality depends on the source, the variables and how representative they are locally.

scale.label: Scale
scale.title: Precise terrain does not imply precise weather
scale.description: The map may show a slope in detail, but the weather data may cover a much larger area. Drawing small cells does not create new measurements.

history.label: History
history.title: The starting point matters
history.description: FWI carries over moisture states from previous days. Initialisation, gaps in the history and the alignment of times affect the result.

updates.label: Updates
updates.title: Data may arrive late
updates.description: A daily assessment does not represent every minute. Delays, revisions or provider failures must be shown alongside the actual date of the data.

scope.label: Scope
scope.title: It does not predict whether a fire will start
scope.description: FWI is not an ignition probability, a fire spread simulation or a complete assessment of people, buildings, fuels and terrain.

decisions.label: Decisions
decisions.title: Official guidance takes priority
decisions.description: A low index does not mean it is safe or authorise burning or other activities. Consult the applicable official restrictions and warnings.
